G2.quote: Every `if err := ...; err != nil` here is `if`-scoped, so it shadows the function-level `err` the defer inspects. If the credit to the destination fails after the debit from the source already succeeded, the outer `err` is still `nil` when the defer runs — it commits instead of rolling back, leaving the source debited with no matching credit or ledger entries.

G3.quote: createPayout (handler.go:150) and createTransfer (transfer.go:46) check acct.BalanceCents loaded earlier in the request, but adjustBalance (store.go:250-264) blindly applies the delta with no floor check. Two concurrent requests can each pass the check and both apply, overdrawing the account

G4.quote: `resp, err := c.post(ctx, body, p.Reference)` ... shadows the outer err ... Send returns (PayoutResult{}, nil) — a fake success with empty ProviderID/Status.

G5.quote: goResult uses an unbuffered channel; waitOrTimeout (handler.go:200-209) abandons it once the timer fires... leaves the spawned goroutine blocked forever on ch <- f() with no receiver.

G6.quote: when ctx.Done() fires during the retry backoff, the function returns without closing resp.Body, leaking the connection.

G7.quote: lookupError has no Unwrap()`, so errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) in writeStoreError (handler.go:252) can't see through it. Every "account/transfer not found" from GetAccount/GetTransfer now falls into the default branch — logged as unexpected and returned as 500 instead of 404.

G9.quote: startOfBusinessDay uses the wrong timezone for the date... y, m, d := now.UTC().Date()   // should be now.In(loc).Date() ... this returns a timestamp *after* now ... sent is always 0 — the daily limit is effectively disabled for that window every day.

D3.quote: Safe today only because maxPayoutCents (25M) is under math.MaxInt32; fragile if that cap ever changes.
